sources.quote: This modelled wind speed didn’t occur at surface Jubilee Line Extension platforms hence the decision was taken not to equip these stations.
The underground stations along this extension are equipped with platform screen doors.
there are no plans to install platform edge doors on Bakerloo line stations.
They are a specialist mechanical element, common to all sub-surface Crossrail Stations.

interpretation: Manual station list cross-checked against the rule for subsurface stations on the 1999 extension and the saved TfL route topology, not an API door attribute.

FOI-0284-2627 says 16 stations on the Jubilee Line Extension. That count conflicts with the 11-station extension: it is not used as a station count or as evidence of doors at surface stations. Eight equipped stations have sixteen directional platforms.
All eight equipped Jubilee stations are in this demo. Green Park predates the 1999 extension. Surface Canning Town, West Ham and Stratford are outside the selected subset.

Crossrail paper confirms doors at all subsurface Crossrail stations and explicitly names its five mined stations. The other underground box stations are Paddington, Canary Wharf and Woolwich; Custom House and Abbey Wood are surface stations. The reference list is documentation only; Elizabeth is not added to the simulation.
Waterloo is shared by Jubilee and Bakerloo. The station-level flag necessarily adds dwell time to Bakerloo too; FOI-0943-2122 confirms this is a model approximation, not the physical situation.
